name: Project Larch
one_liner: Developer-first cloud security that finds misconfigurations in infrastructure-as-code and running accounts and fixes them as code.

buyer.role: VP Engineering, head of DevOps/platform, or cloud-focused CISO
buyer.company_profile: Cloud-native software companies (100-5,000 staff) on AWS/Azure/GCP that manage infrastructure with Terraform or CloudFormation and lack a large cloud security team.

user: DevOps, platform and DevSecOps engineers who own the infrastructure code.

problem.summary: Most cloud breaches come from small misconfigurations (public storage, open ports, missing encryption). Responsibility for infrastructure security has shifted to engineers who define it in code, but security tools alert in runtime consoles built for security teams, creating tickets instead of fixes and inflating the engineering backlog.

evidence.claim: Infrastructure is increasingly defined as code (Terraform, CloudFormation), so the configuration that creates risk lives in repositories.
Terraform is a widely adopted open-source infrastructure-as-code tool spanning multiple clouds.
Misconfigured cloud storage buckets are a recurring source of data exposure.
Cloud security is a shared responsibility in which customers secure their own configuration.

why_now.summary: Infrastructure-as-code has become the default way to provision cloud, so policies can be checked in pull requests and fixes delivered as code. DevOps teams now own security outcomes but existing tools are not developer-friendly.

features.feature: Open-source static scanner for Terraform and CloudFormation with hundreds of built-in policies
features.why: Bottom-up adoption by engineers and a community moat.

features.feature: Runtime scan of cloud accounts with drift detection against the IaC
Automated remediation delivered as pull requests or code snippets
CI/CD and VCS integrations (GitHub, GitLab, Jenkins)

features.why: Gives the security buyer a reason to pay.

competitors.name: Check Point CloudGuard Dome9
competitors.how_we_differ: Built for engineers and code, not a runtime console for security teams.

competitors.name: AWS Config (bundled)
competitors.how_we_differ: Multi-cloud, scans code before deployment and fixes it as code.

competitors.name: Cloud Custodian (free, open source)
competitors.how_we_differ: Pre-deployment IaC scanning plus managed policies and remediation PRs.

competitors.name: Snyk
competitors.how_we_differ: Focus on cloud infrastructure configuration rather than application dependencies.

competitors.name: Prowler (free, open source)
competitors.how_we_differ: Covers code and runtime with automated fixes, not only audit reports.

differentiation: Shift-left by design: one policy set across IaC and runtime, remediation delivered as code, and an open-source scanner that engineers adopt freely before the company buys the platform. Sells to the CISO top-down while engineers pull it in bottom-up.

build.team: About 15 people: security and cloud engineers with prior security-startup founders
hardest_parts: Policy coverage across many cloud resource types and IaC frameworks
Reliable automated fixes that don't break infrastructure
Converting free open-source users to paid
Mapping runtime resources back to the code that created them

pricing.model: Free open-source scanner and free community tier; paid SaaS priced per cloud resource scanned
pricing.entry_price: Working assumption: free up to 100 resources; about $10 per resource per month beyond
pricing.rationale: Low-friction start lets engineers adopt without procurement; per-resource pricing scales with cloud footprint.

comparables.price: No public list price at the time (quote-based enterprise sale)

go_to_market.first_customers: Ten venture-backed cloud-native SaaS companies with Terraform-managed AWS, a small or no security team and a SOC 2 audit coming.
go_to_market.channel: Open-source community (GitHub, DevOps meetups) feeding a self-serve tier, plus direct sales to CISOs.
go_to_market.wedge: Free IaC scanner in CI that flags misconfigurations in pull requests.

risks: Cloud providers bundle native posture checks for free
Open-source users never convert to paid
Larger security platforms add IaC scanning

riskiest_assumption.assumption: Engineering teams will adopt a security scanner in their pipelines voluntarily and their companies will pay for the managed platform.
riskiest_assumption.test: Publish the open-source scanner and measure weekly active CI usage and inbound requests for the paid tier over 2 weeks.
riskiest_assumption.success_signal: At least 500 repositories running the scanner and 10 inbound requests from companies for the paid platform.

open_questions: Who owns the budget: engineering or security?
Will automated remediation be trusted in production?
How defensible is an open-source policy library?
